newsitem.title: USA: SBC, in first joint report, shows higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: SBC, in first joint report, shows higher earnings.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc., in its first report as a merged company after acquiring Pacific Telesis Group, Friday reported higher first quarter earnings.
SBC said its earnings rose to $857 million, or 94 cents a share, on a pro forma basis that reflects the April 1 merger with Pacific Telesis vs. $798 million, or 86 cents a share a year earlier.

San Antonio, Texas-bsaed SBC Communications is the holding company for Southwestern Bell, Pacific Bell, Nevada Bell and Cellular One, and provides local and long-distance telephone service, wireless communications, paging, Internet access, cable TV and messaging.

First-quarter earnings were affected by higher expenses at Pacific Bell, including start-up costs for new wireless services and other growth initiatives, and expenses in the wireline business including preparation for increased competition and unusually high costs associated with damage caused by winter storms.

"SBC's combined first-quarter results reflect strong basic growth trends, with Southwestern Bell's access line gains at historically high levels, continued expansion of demand for data-related products for both residential and business customers, and excellent customer growth in our wireless operations," said Edward Whitacre Jr., chairman and chief executive officer.
The company said revenues increased 7.5 percent to $5.99 billion from $5.57 billion a year earlier on a pro forma basis. The companies reported their first quarters last month on a stand-alone basis.
After the merger, SBC has about 110,000 employees.
